evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database)
evidence.text: The database follows Qiu Xigui in analyzing the early graph as 一 over 刀, with 一 marking the blade’s edge, and says 方 was borrowed for the square sense. It gives competing readings: a knife hanging on a rack (Ye Yusen), an early 枋 with a mark at the holding point (Zhu Fangpu), a 耒-like implement (Xu Zhongshu), or a knife dividing something (He Linyi). These are scholarly interpretations; the database does not establish the depicted object beyond dispute.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：方

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database)
evidence.text: The database reports oracle-bone examples of 方 for a western direction (合集 28190), a four-direction ritual (合集 30394), polities (合集 36536; 屯南 2301), and polity leaders (合集 28086). It says oracle and bronze forms are broadly similar; variant upper strokes include an inverted 工-like form and an added short stroke. The page provides no precise dates for these individual tokens, and the forms’ variation alone does not prove a corruption sequence.
evidence.kind: secondary scholarly dictionary citing inscription numbers
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：方

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database)
evidence.text: The database cites Western Zhou bronze uses for square shape (史逨方鼎), land measurement (召卣), direction (不𡢁𣪕), and polity (人方). It cites a 中山王鼎 adverbial use glossed “just/now” and Shuihudi Qin slip 131 for 方 as a writing board. The source gives no absolute dates for these examples and does not establish a semantic chain among them.
evidence.kind: secondary scholarly dictionary citing inscriptions and excavated text
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：方

evidence.source: 《說文解字》 online transcription and 段玉裁 commentary
evidence.text: The received Shuowen entry defines 方 as paired boats and explains its shape as abbreviated boats with their heads together. Duan Yucai’s later commentary treats raft, comparison, square/round, uprightness, and direction as extensions. This is historical lexicographic interpretation, not direct proof of the graph’s original referent or of a dated semantic sequence.
evidence.kind: primary historical dictionary transcription with later commentary
evidence.title: 說文解字「方」

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry reproduces the paired-boats Shuowen definition and Duan commentary. It lists senses including parallel arrangement, comparison, square shape, uprightness, region, direction, method, medicine prescription, and temporal adverbial meanings, with received-text citations. The dictionary lists these senses and citations, but does not date their development.
evidence.title: A01759 方 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: William H. Baxter and Laurent Sagart
evidence.text: The Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese table lists modern Mandarin fāng and Middle Chinese transcription pjang for 方, reconstructing *C-paŋ for “square” and *paŋ for “method” and “just, then.” The authors say their Middle Chinese notation represents readings in sources such as Guangyun rather than a reconstruction; Old Chinese forms are reconstructions, not direct records of Shang speech.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1

evidence.field: Zhengzhang pronunciation and variant comparison systems
evidence.text: The entry gives 方 as *paŋ in the Zhengzhang system, Yang rhyme group, and lists several Middle Chinese reconstructions from other named systems. These are system-specific historical reconstructions; it does not independently prove the proposed pictured object or its name.
evidence.title: 方 — 上古音系

evidence.text: The page places 方 and 旁 in a broad 方 series and reports Zhengzhang-style Old Chinese *paŋ/*baŋ for 方 and *baːŋ for 旁. This supports a possible later phonetic role for 方 in 旁 given historical sound similarity. It does not establish that 方 was 旁’s original graph, that the words are cognate, or the earliest compound reading. Its side-by-side historical series is secondary compilation, not direct paleographic proof.
evidence.title: 方 - 维基词典，自由的多语言词典

evidence.field: oracle-style glyph file description and rights
evidence.text: The Commons page identifies 方-oracle.svg as 方 in an oracle-script style, identifies a source image in the hanziyuan.net dataset and related reference databases, and marks the digital vector representation public domain. The file is a modern digital drawing, not an ancient artifact photograph.
evidence.title: File:方-oracle.svg

gaps: The earliest depicted object for 方 remains disputed among a marked blade/edge, knife/rack, knife handle, dividing tool, 耒-like implement, paddle/oar, or the Shuowen paired-boats account. The object’s spoken name and pronunciation are not independently recoverable, so no borrowing argument that requires that name is established.
The blade/edge-to-square borrowing proposal is a scholarly analysis. No inspected primary inscription proves the depicted object’s name or the sound relation required by that account.

The Shang inscriptions are reported through the CUHK database with corpus numbers, but accessible direct facsimiles and full primary transcriptions were not inspected. Exact reign/year dating of the cited tokens is unavailable in the inspected account.
Shang direction, polity, place, ritual, and later square, method, and temporal uses are not established here as a dated semantic chain. Gloss order in dictionaries is not chronology.
Received-text citations in the variants dictionary are not securely dated manuscript attestations for each sense; the absolute earliest instance of each sense remains undetermined.
方 and 旁 may share historical phonetic material, but the evidence inspected does not prove 旁’s original graph was 方, cognacy, or the earliest phonetic value in the compound.

Xiaoxuetang’s 方 query page did not expose result labels or direct image URLs in browser extraction, so no image was selected from that service. No image pixels were inspected in this research stage; the Commons candidates are identified from their source descriptions only.
Unrelated dossier notes about dialectal 慌, 仿 variant usage, and English phon were not independently verified as historical formation evidence.

The labels identify script styles and source datasets; they do not settle the original referent or establish the chronology of all graphic variants.
